what: Telkom Indonesia is the country's largest telecom operator. Its Telkomsel arm is the biggest mobile network, and it also provides fixed broadband, data centres and enterprise connectivity.
customers: Indonesian households and businesses, mostly on prepaid mobile and IndiHome broadband.
money: corporate connectivity, towers and data centres
moat: A network reaching across an archipelago of thousands of islands, built over decades with state backing, which no competitor can match for coverage.
risks: Indonesian mobile pricing has been competitive and revenue per user is low
The state is the controlling shareholder and its priorities are not purely commercial
Only one analyst covers the American listing
opportunities: 12 times earnings and 5.3 times free cash flow with $2.1B of free cash flow
A 11.9% net margin and $2.1B of cash against $2.3B of debt
Indonesian broadband penetration is still low and data use per subscriber keeps rising
watch: Telkomsel's revenue per subscriber and IndiHome broadband additions.
